name: PEOPLE
aliases: Pessary or Surgery for Pelvic Organ Prolapse
question: Is initial pessary treatment noninferior to prolapse surgery for patient-reported improvement at 24 months?

design.blinding: Open-label; participants and treating gynecologists were not masked
design.population: Women referred to 21 Dutch hospitals with symptomatic POP-Q stage 2 or greater prolapse, moderate to severe symptoms, a successful 30-minute pessary fitting trial, and no prior prolapse or incontinence surgery or pessary use.
design.locator: JAMA full text, Methods: Participants, Randomization and Interventions; Results: Trial Population

verdictNote: Neither as-randomized nor per-protocol analysis met the 10-point noninferiority margin.
takeaway: In symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse, initial pessary treatment did not meet the prespecified noninferiority criterion versus surgery for patient-reported improvement at 24 months; 54.1% of those assigned pessary crossed over to surgery.

reports.label: 24-month randomized report
reports.citation: van der Vaart LR, Vollebregt A, Milani AL, et al. "Effect of Pessary vs Surgery on Patient-Reported Improvement in Patients With Symptomatic Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2022;328(23):2312-2323.
reports.followUp: 24 months; primary outcome available for 173/218 pessary and 162/221 eligible surgery participants
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA full text, abstract and Results: Trial Population; Figure 1

results.measure: PGI-I much or very much better at 24 months; risk difference in percentage points, pessary minus surgery, as-randomized respondents
results.note: One-sided 95% CI lower bound −12.7 percentage points crossed the prespecified −10-point margin; P is for noninferiority.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Results: Primary Outcomes; Table 2

results.measure: PGI-I much or very much better at 24 months; risk difference in percentage points, pessary minus surgery, per-protocol respondents

delivery.label: Treating clinician experience
delivery.value: Each participating gynecologist had previously fitted at least 100 pessaries and performed at least 100 vaginal prolapse operations.

delivery.label: Pessary treatment and follow-up
delivery.value: Supportive or occlusive pessaries; refitting offered after expulsion; cleaning or clinician visit at least every 4 months.

delivery.label: Surgical technique
delivery.value: Gynecologist-selected vaginal compartment repair, hysterectomy or uterine preservation for uterine descent; abdominal sacrocolpopexy permitted; no concomitant stress-incontinence surgery.
